marble_dark.notes: Polished near-black marble with thin gold-white veins. Low roughness (~0.17) and a very weak normal, so it reads as polished. Albedo kept dark (mean ~0.12 sRGB). Organic pattern, so repetition is barely visible. Floors and wall cladding in ancient interiors.

stone_pale.notes: Pale white-gold limestone ashlar, 5 courses per tile (blocks about 1.0 x 0.5 m at 2.5 m/tile). Courses run along U; on walls, map V to up. Rough (~0.8). Regular bond, so the repeat is visible on very large flat walls; break it with trims or decals. Ancient precursor architecture, parapets, plazas.

stone_worn.notes: Dark charcoal worn flagstones of varied size, with black grime in the joints (rougher and AO-darkened). Slab tops are smoother (~0.62) and the joints rougher. Floors, roads, courtyards.

bronze_plate.notes: Aged, scored bronze with engraved flame-like ornament in shallow grooves (a darker patina in the grooves gives higher roughness and AO). Fully metallic, roughness ~0.45. At tiled scale the ornament reads softly and the surface looks partly hammered or mottled. Use 0.5-1.0 m/tile on props and armour and 1.5-3 m on large wall or hull plates. Dominion structures and set-dressing.

panel_navy.notes: Deep navy hull plating in panels of varied size, with thin light seams and a few silver trim strips. The height was inverted, so panels are raised and seams and strips recessed. Metalness 0.8 on the navy paint and 1.0 on the silver trim, roughness ~0.36. With the ORM metalness it reads dark in dim scenes: lift material.color or envMapIntensity rather than the map. Reformation interiors and hulls; use 8-20 m/tile on large distant hulls.

metal_blackgold.notes: Aged blackened metal with a light rust bloom and bright gold inlay lines in a chevron pattern (about 4 chevron columns per tile; the chevrons point along -V). Fully metallic. The gold lines are smoother (lower roughness) and very slightly raised. Ancient black-gold relics, doors, plinths, trims.

frost.notes: Feathery white frost crystals over dark grey stone; the crystals are slightly smoother than the stone. Organic, so the repeat is not obvious. Use as a frost overlay or blend layer on stone, or on its own for icy floors.

eclipse_tissue.notes: Black wet organic membrane with branching violet veins. Roughness ~0.32 (wet), and the baked glints from the source were suppressed. Extra map: emissive.webp is a violet vein mask (sRGB). Use material.emissiveMap with emissive=0xffffff and emissiveIntensity 1-3, and pulse it for life. Corruption surfaces.

concrete_hangar.notes: Worn grey steel and concrete hangar deck in a 6x6 grid of plates per tile (1 m plates at 6 m/tile), with corner bolts, scuffs, oil stains and faint tyre marks. The tyre marks repeat visibly on very large floors, so overlay decals. Metal is false as the brief asked; it reads as painted or sealed deck. Hangars, landing pads, industrial floors.
